answer: A bonded identity vault resists sybils: before earning, each identity must lock a separate, non-transferable bond in a vault, released only after a full epoch of honest attestation. If the same operator's duplicate signal — identical timing, parents, or attestation pattern — appears under two identities, both bonds are slashed. An attacker running a thousand sockpuppets must lock a thousand bonds, tying up capital that earns nothing, and each detected duplicate forfeits real money, not a free retry. Cost scales with fakes, as a sable pelt cannot be photocopied.
